summary: Bend reaches the outside world only through IO: a CPS type over IO.OP{Emit|Halt}, where every effect is a def whose body is two imports (.c and .js) registered with io_eff. The JS lane is Bun-centric (Bun.spawnSync, bun:ffi libc). Surface: print/env/args/process/random/sleep/now/chan/file/tcp/udp/window/audio. No HTTP, DNS or JSON; the demos hand-build HTTP over TCP strings. Three embedding routes: Bun.plugin, node mod.register hook, and ahead-of-time `-o x.mjs`. All three go through book_read, so the full checker runs on import or emit (verified: a type error and an affine error both refused). Node 20 cannot load the .ts loader (ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION); `-o x.mjs` then works under node 20. Data shape across the boundary: constructors `{$:"Name", field}`, Nat BigInt at the edge but JS Number inside (capped at 2^48-1), String/Bool/U32 native, Maybe/Result/Tuple as tagged objects, curried exports. Docs CLAIM only non-IO defs export; code DOES export IO defs with ≥1 parameter (filter inspects the whole function type) and exports filled proofs, which compile to `return null`. Exported IO defs cannot run from the .mjs: the event loop and io_out live in RUNTIME_MAIN, which js_lib omits. --verdict passed on the experiment.

facts.claim: IO is a continuation type over IO.OP: `def IO(-A: Type) -> Type: @-R: Type -> @k: (A -> IO.OP<R>) -> IO.OP<R>`; IO.OP has two constructors Emit{value: R} and Halt{code: U32, message: String}; IO.pure and IO.bind are plain defs over it.
facts.quote:
Emit{value: R}
  Halt{code: U32, message: String}

facts.claim: Every Base effect is a def whose body is two imports, one .c and one .js (e.g. IO.print, Process.run, File.open, Chan.new). Fallible effects answer `Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, A>`; handle effects return the handle beside the result, e.g. File.read -> `IO(File & Result<...>)`.
Handles (File, Socket, Listener, Window, Audio) are laws of kind Type with no constructor; the comment states no program forges, copies or reuses one. Chan is a law of kind Data (copyable).
facts.quote:
A handle is opaque, a law with no constructor and no field, so no
# program forges one, and linear (Type), so none copies or reuses one.

facts.claim: EFFECTS.md documents the JS effect calling convention: 'a U32 is a number, a Nat a BigInt, a String a string, a constructor {$: CID(Name), field: value}, a handle its host value'; answers via io_done(v), io_fail(code), io_tup(handle, result), {$: CID(Unit)}. Blocking effects take a k and park with io_park_on; io_sys() is libc through bun:ffi.
EFFECTS.md says the effect ABI tracks the exact compiler version: 'There is no ABI promise. Rebuild your effects with every update.' (document is self-described as AI-written from source).

Runtime JS helpers define the cross-boundary shapes: io_fail -> `{ $: "Fail", error: io_tup(code >>> 0, io_strerror(code)) }`, io_done -> `{ $: "Done", value }`, io_tup -> nested `{ $: "Tuple", fst, snd }`.
In emitted JS, CID(Name) expands to the name string: the module registers `io_eff("IO.print", io_print)` and guards `for (const k of ["IO.print"]) { if (!(k in $0eff)) throw ... }`.

GUIDE: custom effects are allowed the same way; 'Only the event loop runs them, so proofs, termination and the GPU never touch host code.' JS may import a .bend (loader preloaded) or the -o .mjs 'and call every non-IO def, with constructors as {$: "Name", field: value} and Nat as BigInt'; 'A value crosses without a copy: an Array argument is the caller's own array, updated in place'.
WONTFIX: a user-defined handle type is not allowed; a custom effect must reuse a Base handle law (File, Socket, Window...).

Export filter in js_lib: `done_live(t) && !def_foreign(t) && t.b !== true && t.x === 0 && io_base(book, t.T) === null`. `b` is the base flag; `x` counts `~` template binders (parser sets `x: tk.length`).

io_base wnf's the WHOLE type and tests whether its head is Ref IO; a function type (All) has no such head, so an IO def with one or more parameters passes the non-IO filter. CODE DOES export such defs; the header and GUIDE CLAIM non-IO only.

CAPTURED: z.mjs exported `[ 'greet', 'twice' ]` and excluded zero-arg `hello() -> IO(Unit)`; x.mjs exported `[ 'area2', 'label', 'pick', 'area2_circle', 'greet' ]` including the IO def greet(name) and the proof area2_circle.

CAPTURED: calling an exported IO def from node returns a function; applying a continuation yields `{ '$': '$FFI', run: [Function: io_print], need: undefined, args: [ 'hi bob' ], kont: [Function] }`; invoking run throws 'ReferenceError: io_out is not defined'. So an IO def is callable but not runnable from the .mjs.

facts.claim: js_lib emits RUNTIME + effect sources + program + export block; js_book appends RUNTIME_MAIN plus cli/io_exit. io_out (6136), io_sys (6159), io_push (6248), io_park_on (6292) and the event loop io_run (6298) are all inside RUNTIME_MAIN (starts 6050), so the .mjs has no event loop (grep count of io_run/io_push in x.mjs and z.mjs: 0).
The in-process runner is Comp.io_run(book, args): it builds `new Function("require", js_lib(book) + RUNTIME_MAIN + ...)` and runs main; this is how `bend file.bend` executes IO under Bun.
The event loop drives `$FFI` ops: `op.run(...op.args, op.kont)`, then `op = op.kont(x)`; Emit ends a computation, Halt exits with code; need.time/need.read parks via io_park_on.

Export wrapper (js_host): each live argument is in-marshalled, the def is run through run_loop, the result out-marshalled, then the in-marshal is reversed on the arguments (`back`) — the generated form: `"area2": run_lib((a0) => { const r = BigInt(run_loop($area2$($0m0(a0)))); $0m1(a0); return r; }, 1)`; args without Nat fields pass through untouched: `"pick": run_lib((a0, a1, a2) => { const r = (run_loop($pick$((a0), (a1), (a2)))); ... }, 3)`.

Nat is BigInt only at the boundary: nat_host accepts a bigint OR an integer Number <= 2^53 and converts to Number; nat_chk throws 'a Nat past the largest immediate 2^48-1' above 281474976710655. CAPTURED: a JS number 4 for a Nat field was accepted (area2 -> 12n); results come back as BigInt (12n, 15n, 42n).
facts.quote: throw "bend: a Nat past the largest immediate 2^48-1";

facts.claim: Concurrency model (GUIDE): one event loop interleaving computations 'as in Node.js'; IO.fork/IO.join over Chan; IO.within races against a deadline, 'the loser is not cancelled'; the program 'reports a deadlock when the remaining ones all wait'. io_run returns 1 on 'deadlock: every computation waits on a channel'.

open_questions: Does node >= 22.6 (built-in TypeScript type stripping) accept `node --import bend2/main.ts` as the README claims? Only node 20 was available; the hook itself (main.ts 885-891, mod.register 905-906) is plain, so it may work there.
Is exporting IO defs with parameters (greet) from -o .mjs intended, or a defect in io_base's whole-type check (comp.ts 1273-1283)? The header, GUIDE and the zero-arg exclusion all say non-IO only.

How would a TypeScript host run an exported IO def? The .mjs lacks RUNTIME_MAIN (event loop, io_out, io_sys via bun:ffi, Bun.spawnSync in process_run.js). Options untested: `-o x.js` full program under node; calling Comp.io_run from a Bun process; writing a host driver for the $FFI op protocol.
Does the Bun/node loader cache compiled .bend output between imports or processes? load_js (main.ts 877-883) shows no cache; cost of a full check per import is unmeasured.
Constructor tags depend on the loading file's view of a name (TODO #1105, comp.ts 3165-3167): can a server and a Bend module disagree on tags when modules are nested or aliased?
The JS lane caps Nat at 2^48-1 (x.mjs 28-33) and accepts a JS Number where the docs say BigInt; is any fidelity counter or hash likely to exceed that?

Bool arguments are not validated (truthiness, x.mjs 201); untagged List/String arguments bypass tag checks; is the boundary's lack of input validation acceptable for a fidelity use, or must the TS side validate shapes first?
The HTTP demos are hand-rolled over TCP with no DNS/TLS; is any network reach from Bend needed, or would all IO stay on the TS side with Bend as a pure library?
